has_subtypes.description: The PSMB8-associated form and the reference presentation of the umbrella disease. Recessive variants in the inducible beta-5i catalytic subunit cause CANDLE, and the same gene underlies the JMP presentation curated in this entry. Per-gene detail is in the PSMB8 record of the genetic section.

evidence.explanation: The discovery study establishes PSMB8 as causative for the JMP presentation, one of the historically named phenotypes this subtype row covers.
evidence.reference_title: PSMB8 encoding the β5i proteasome subunit is mutated in joint contractures, muscle atrophy, microcytic anemia, and panniculitis-induced lipodystrophy syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We conclude that mutations in PSMB8 cause JMP syndrome, most probably by affecting MHC class I antigen processing.

genes.description: Encodes the inducible immunoproteasome catalytic subunit beta-5i. Recessive loss-of-function variants are the founding PRAAS genotype and the one the dominant and digenic architectures were recognised against.

evidence.explanation: States the recessive architecture of the PSMB8-associated form directly.
evidence.reference_title: Additive loss-of-function proteasome subunit mutations in CANDLE/PRAAS patients promote type I IFN production.
evidence.snippet: Autosomal recessive mutations in proteasome subunit β 8 (PSMB8), which encodes the inducible proteasome subunit β5i, cause the immune-dysregulatory disease chronic atypical neutrophilic dermatosis with lipodystrophy and elevated temperature (CANDLE)

has_subtypes.name: PRAAS1

has_subtypes.description: The POMP-associated form, distinguished by early-onset combined immunodeficiency alongside the inflammatory neutrophilic dermatosis and autoimmunity. Its discovery study named it POMP-related autoinflammation and immune dysregulation disease (PRAID). PRAAS2 is the name MONDO:0054700 carries as a synonym, mapped to OMIM:618048.

evidence.explanation: Names the PRAAS2 entity and its defining features, which is what this subtype row asserts.
evidence.reference_title: Proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome 2 in a neonate.
evidence.snippet: Proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome-2 (PRAAS2) is characterized by early onset combined immunodeficiency, inflammatory neutrophilic dermatosis, and autoimmunity.

evidence.explanation: Ties the PRAAS2 diagnosis to a de novo POMP frameshift variant in a further, independent patient.
evidence.reference_title: Proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome 2 in a neonate.
evidence.snippet: A novel de novo frameshift proteasome maturation protein (POMP) mutation (c.333delT (p.t111fs)) was detected, confirming the diagnosis.

evidence.explanation: The discovery study's own naming of the POMP entity, and the clinical constellation that distinguishes it inside the PRAAS spectrum.
evidence.reference_title: Heterozygous Truncating Variants in POMP Escape Nonsense-Mediated Decay and Cause a Unique Immune Dysregulatory Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Here, we characterize and describe POMP-related autoinflammation and immune dysregulation disease (PRAID) discovered in two unrelated individuals with a unique constellation of early-onset combined immunodeficiency, inflammatory neutrophilic dermatosis, and autoimmunity.

genes.description: Encodes proteasome maturation protein, a chaperone for proteasome assembly that is critical for incorporating the catalytic subunits. The reported disease variants are frameshifts in the penultimate exon that escape nonsense-mediated decay and act by a dominant-negative mechanism, so this is an assembly-chaperone defect rather than a proteasome-subunit defect.

inheritance.description: A single heterozygous POMP variant is sufficient, acting by a dominant-negative mechanism on proteasome assembly.

evidence.explanation: Reports both the de novo heterozygous architecture and the dominant-negative mechanism that makes one allele sufficient.
evidence.reference_title: Heterozygous Truncating Variants in POMP Escape Nonsense-Mediated Decay and Cause a Unique Immune Dysregulatory Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: de novo heterozygous frameshift variants in the penultimate exon of POMP escape nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) and result in a truncated protein that perturbs proteasome assembly by a dominant-negative mechanism

evidence.explanation: Independent report of a single heterozygous POMP variant in a PRAAS patient, cited for the dominant arm it establishes.
evidence.reference_title: Additive loss-of-function proteasome subunit mutations in CANDLE/PRAAS patients promote type I IFN production.
evidence.snippet: 1 patient was heterozygous for a POMP mutation, thus establishing a digenic and autosomal dominant inheritance pattern of PRAAS

inheritance.name: Autosomal dominant, de novo

has_subtypes.name: PRAAS2

has_subtypes.description: The PSMB4-associated form. PSMB4 was one of four proteasome genes newly linked to CANDLE/PRAAS by the additive loss-of-function study, which reported it both as a compound-heterozygous cause in one patient and as a constitutive subunit participating in digenic genotypes.

evidence.explanation: The study that first associated PSMB4 with the disease, naming the subunit it encodes.
evidence.reference_title: Additive loss-of-function proteasome subunit mutations in CANDLE/PRAAS patients promote type I IFN production.
evidence.snippet: we identified 8 mutations in 4 proteasome genes, PSMA3 (encodes α7), PSMB4 (encodes β7), PSMB9 (encodes β1i), and proteasome maturation protein (POMP), that have not been previously associated with disease

genes.description: Encodes the beta-7 subunit of the constitutive 20S proteasome. Beta-7 is a structural subunit of the beta-ring, not one of the three catalytic active site subunits. PSMB4 is reported both as a biallelic cause and as a constitutive-component partner in the digenic architecture this entry curates.

evidence.explanation: A compound-heterozygous genotype in a single patient, which is the recessive architecture of this form.
evidence.reference_title: Additive loss-of-function proteasome subunit mutations in CANDLE/PRAAS patients promote type I IFN production.
evidence.snippet: One patient was compound heterozygous for PSMB4 mutations

has_subtypes.name: PRAAS3

has_subtypes.description: The PSMG2-associated form, reported in a patient with CANDLE features who also had autoimmune hemolytic anemia. PSMG2 encodes the PAC2 assembly chaperone, making this the second chaperone-defect form alongside PRAAS2.

evidence.explanation: Establishes PSMG2 as a cause of the CANDLE presentation curated by this entry.
evidence.reference_title: Novel proteasome assembly chaperone mutations in PSMG2/PAC2 cause the autoinflammatory interferonopathy CANDLE/PRAAS4.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in the proteasome chaperone, PSMG2/PAC2 are a novel cause of CANDLE.

genes.description: Encodes proteasome assembly chaperone 2 (PAC2). Like POMP this is an assembly-chaperone defect rather than a proteasome-subunit defect, which is why the two are wired to the chaperone node of the pathograph.

has_subtypes.name: PRAAS4

has_subtypes.description: The PSMB10-associated form. Compound-heterozygous PSMB10 variants were found in three unrelated Brazilian patients with a CANDLE/PRAAS phenotype, and the variants were shown to block incorporation of the beta-2i subunit into mature proteasomes.

evidence.explanation: Names PSMB10 as an established CANDLE/PRAAS gene and reports the genotypes this row is keyed on.
evidence.reference_title: Identification of eight novel proteasome variants in five unrelated cases of proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndromes (PRAAS).
evidence.snippet: Four patients were compound heterozygous for novel pathogenic variants in the known CANDLE/PRAAS associated genes, PSMB8 and PSMB10

evidence.explanation: Functional evidence that the reported variants act by impairing subunit expression or incorporation, the mechanism this entry models downstream.
evidence.reference_title: Identification of eight novel proteasome variants in five unrelated cases of proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndromes (PRAAS).
evidence.snippet: All newly identified mutations substantially impact the steady-state expression of the affected proteasome subunits and/or their incorporation into mature 26S proteasomes.

genes.description: Encodes the inducible immunoproteasome catalytic subunit beta-2i (MECL1), the third inducible subunit alongside beta-5i (PSMB8) and beta-1i (PSMB9).

evidence.explanation: Compound heterozygosity across the reported patients is the recessive architecture of this form.
evidence.reference_title: Identification of eight novel proteasome variants in five unrelated cases of proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndromes (PRAAS).
evidence.snippet: Four patients were compound heterozygous for novel pathogenic variants in the known CANDLE/PRAAS associated genes, PSMB8 and PSMB10

has_subtypes.name: PRAAS5

has_subtypes.description: The PSMB9-associated form. This row is the most contested in the series. The two reported patients carried the same de novo heterozygous PSMB9 G156D variant and had pulmonary hypertension and combined immunodeficiency without lipoatrophy, and their authors proposed a separate category, PRAAS-ID, rather than a PRAAS subtype. MONDO:0968983 instead labels it proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome 6, maps it to OMIM:620796 and places it directly under this umbrella, which is the nosology this row follows; the countervailing argument is recorded here and in the entry notes.

evidence.explanation: Supports PSMB9 variants producing a PRAAS-like disease while naming the two features that separate it from the rest of the spectrum.
evidence.reference_title: Heterozygous missense variant of the proteasome subunit β-type 9 causes neonatal-onset autoinflammation and immunodeficiency.
evidence.snippet: In addition to PRAAS-like manifestations, these individuals suffer from pulmonary hypertension and immunodeficiency, which are distinct from typical PRAAS symptoms.

evidence.explanation: Cited against this row's placement: the reporting authors argue the PSMB9 entity is a separate category rather than a PRAAS subtype.
evidence.reference_title: Heterozygous missense variant of the proteasome subunit β-type 9 causes neonatal-onset autoinflammation and immunodeficiency.
evidence.snippet: We propose the term, proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome with immunodeficiency (PRAAS-ID), to indicate a separate category of autoinflammatory diseases, similar to, but distinct from PRAAS, that describes the patients in this study.

evidence.explanation: PSMB9 was first linked to CANDLE/PRAAS in this cohort, which is the basis for treating the gene as part of the umbrella spectrum.
evidence.reference_title: Additive loss-of-function proteasome subunit mutations in CANDLE/PRAAS patients promote type I IFN production.
evidence.snippet: we identified 8 mutations in 4 proteasome genes, PSMA3 (encodes α7), PSMB4 (encodes β7), PSMB9 (encodes β1i), and proteasome maturation protein (POMP), that have not been previously associated with disease

genes.description: Encodes the inducible immunoproteasome catalytic subunit beta-1i. The reported disease variant is a recurrent de novo heterozygous missense change at glycine 156 that sits on the beta-ring interface.

evidence.explanation: Reports the de novo heterozygous architecture in both patients.
evidence.reference_title: Heterozygous missense variant of the proteasome subunit β-type 9 causes neonatal-onset autoinflammation and immunodeficiency.
evidence.snippet: Here we report a de novo heterozygous missense variant of the PSMB9 proteasome subunit gene in two unrelated Japanese infants resulting in amino acid substitution of the glycine (G) by aspartic acid (D) at position 156 of the encoded protein β1i.

has_subtypes.name: PRAAS6

omimps_mappings.mapping_justification: The January 2026 OMIM snapshot enumerates the six numbered PRAAS forms already represented by this entry's grounded subtypes: OMIM:256040, OMIM:618048, OMIM:617591, OMIM:619183, OMIM:619175 and OMIM:620796. This aligns the named umbrella with the phenotypic series, rather than with the individual PRAAS1 record sharing its number. It does not settle the clinical lumping debate for PRAAS6 or imply a single inheritance pattern across the proteasome and assembly-factor defects.

This aligns the named umbrella with the phenotypic series, rather than with the individual PRAAS1 record sharing its number. It does not settle the clinical lumping debate for PRAAS6 or imply a single inheritance pattern across the proteasome and assembly-factor defects.
